figures_added.what: Area model for completing the square: an x-by-x square (x^2), two 3-by-x strips added to the right and bottom, and a dashed 3x3 corner (area 9) needed to finish the (x+3)^2 square. Theme-safe (currentColor text/strokes, soft fills at 0.3 opacity), drawn roughly to scale, aria-labelled.

notes: Exam-realism judgement: every bank problem is purely algebraic (find the discriminant, complete the square, apply the quadratic formula, sum of roots, discriminant conditions, turning point). Eduqas/GCSE exams print NO figure for these; a parabola sketch on the turning-point (gold[4]), how-many-roots (bronze[7]) or root-finding (silver) problems would reveal the answer visually and undermine the drill, so none was added. The single legitimate figure is the completing-the-square area model, which carries the opener's 'show what you say' claim. No question text, solution, guided step, hint or misconception changed in this pass.
